name: traffic-jam-ramp-head
description: #1208: traffic jams are detected by position at chokepoints, not by shared destination. Dig a ramp, send a crew member on foot to one tile in its body, then send four crewed vehicles to the same tile; once they stall a queue raises the traffic_jam event (trafficJamCount 1, kind ramp_head, rampId 1), and the player answers it by clicking Widen ramp in the event dialog, which orders the widening exactly once. Contract for console-api state (implementer adds): trafficJamCount, trafficJams [{kind, rampId}]. A queue of walkers alone raises the event too; that case is unit-tested (TrafficJams.test.ts), because a walker may step past a vehicle (#1263), so a crew sent after the haulers squeezes by rather than queuing.

steps.description: #1413-followup: cash:100000 so a costly random event answered at the earlier no-op event steps (follow-up events are now queue-only, which shifts which random event lands) cannot leave the mine unable to afford the Widen ramp answer later.

expect.note: trafficJamCount is the #1208 console-state field (implementer adds it); no jam on a fresh site.

steps.description: Staffed vehicles come unmanned (#551) — crew rock_digger #3 with driver #4, one of the two driving.excavator-qualified drivers STARTING_SITE_STAFFED_COMPOSITION grants, before ordering any excavation work. Mirrors ramp-navigation.json's own crewing step.

Same geometry as ramp-navigation.json: a 10m, RAMP_WIDTH=3-wide corridor running south from (15,15). depth:5 keeps every per-column step within NAV_MAX_SLOPE_RATIO and RAMP_CUT_SLOPE_RATIO (#1151/#1152) — see that file's own note for the full derivation. Ordering only queues dig_ramp_segment work; the crewed rock_digger below carves it over the following ticks.
Drain every queued dig_ramp_segment layer — the crewed rock_digger (vehicle #3, driver #4) clears one bench at a time until the whole corridor is carved end to end and walkable.

expect.note: Ramp fully dug: every dig_ramp_segment layer landed.

steps.description: Ramp is dug. Crew the idle vehicles with the licensed drivers: hauler #2 with driver #3, fragmenter #4 with driver #4, drill rig #1 with driller #1 (rock_digger #3 is already crewed and parked at the ramp foot (15,24)). Crewing choices come from the licence table: #5 and #3 cannot drive the fragmenter, #1 only the drill rig.
Let every driver walk to and board their vehicle before the convergence.

A spontaneous random event can fire during the preceding tick batch; a pending event halts ticking in the browser (isPaused), so the staging and the jam wait below would never advance. Resolved through the dialog's own buttons when one is pending; a no-op otherwise.
Stage blaster #2, the one crew member on foot, at the ramp head beside the vehicles, so it reaches the convergence tile ahead of them.

Stage all four vehicles side by side at the ramp head (15,17) area so they start the final run together, instead of trickling in from the depot one at a time (a staggered arrival never has three waiting at once).
Let every vehicle reach its staging tile.

A spontaneous random event can fire during the preceding tick batch; a pending event halts ticking in the browser (isPaused), so the staging and the jam wait below would never advance. Resolved through the dialog's own buttons when one is pending; a no-op otherwise.
The crew member walks down the ramp first and takes the convergence tile; the haulers sent next queue behind it.
Let the crew member reach the tile before the vehicles set off.

A spontaneous random event can fire during the preceding tick batch; a pending event halts ticking in the browser (isPaused), so the staging and the jam wait below would never advance. Resolved through the dialog's own buttons when one is pending; a no-op otherwise.

Convergence: all four vehicles sent together to the ramp-body tile the crew member already holds; they queue single-file behind it. The jam needs TRAFFIC_JAM_MIN_TICKS < AGENT_OCCUPANCY_WAIT_TICKS, otherwise the occupancy ladder spreads the queue before three agents have waited long enough.

Advance simulation time through the console until the stall passes TRAFFIC_JAM_MIN_TICKS: ticking halts on the traffic_jam event itself. Not a waitUntil: waitUntil auto-resolves a pending event after each tick (choose 0 = Reroute Convoy) and would clear the very jam this step must observe. A browser clock is also ~6s/frame without a GPU. The converging vehicles stall at the ramp body; the detector reports exactly one ramp_head jam on ramp 1 and the event is pending.

expect.note: Contract for the console state schema (implementer adds): trafficJamCount = findTrafficJams(...).length ignoring silence; trafficJams = [{kind, rampId}].

steps.description: Player answers the traffic-jam dialog through its own buttons: option 2 of 3 is Widen ramp (index 1). The widen order is charged once and queues the extra excavation; the ramp is silenced so the jam does not immediately re-fire.

expect.note: Exact cost is asserted by TrafficJamEvents.test.ts; here the player-visible claim is that the click lands an order.

steps.description: Player dismisses the outcome card so the scene behind it is visible: the jam marker at the ramp head is unsilenced, so it stays up while the queue still stands.
Wait for the extra side strip to be dug; the built ramp is then 5 wide.
